fullPassage: The history of political philosophy in the West can be traced back to ancient Greece. The term polis, from which is derived the word political, refers to the city-state, the basic unit of government in ancient Greece. Early inquiries were concerned with questions such as “Which qualities make for the best leader?” “Which is the best system of government for a city-state?” and “What is the role of a citizen?” For many philosophers, the most fundamental moral questions—such as “How should I treat others?” and “What constitutes a good life?”—are the basis for corollary political considerations. The philosopher Aristotle (384–322 BCE) links the two through the concept of telos, which means “goal directed.” All things in life have a goal, or an end purpose, he says. It is the goal of human beings to live a good life, which is only achievable by living a life. Acquiring virtue is a difficult task, requiring constant practice. The acquisition of virtue necessarily involves a community to provide education, virtues, and provide opportunities for a person to behave virtuously. According to Aristotle, society is an essential part of living a good life, which involves a well-constructed political life: “This truth is attested by the experience of states: lawgivers make the citizens good by training them in habits of right action—this is the aim of all legislation, and if it fails to do this it is a failure; this is what distinguishes a good form of constitution from a bad one” (1996, 1103b20).

Early inquiries were concerned with questions such as “Which qualities make for the best leader?” “Which is the best system of government for a city-state?” and “What is the role of a citizen?” For many philosophers, the most fundamental moral questions—such as “How should I treat others?” and “What constitutes a good life?”—are the basis for corollary political considerations. The philosopher Aristotle (384–322 BCE) links the two through the concept of telos, which means “goal directed.” All things in life have a goal, or an end purpose, he says. It is the goal of human beings to live a good life, which is only achievable by living a life. Acquiring virtue is a difficult task, requiring constant practice. The acquisition of virtue necessarily involves a community to provide education, virtues, and provide opportunities for a person to behave virtuously. According to Aristotle, society is an essential part of living a good life, which involves a well-constructed political life: “This truth is <u>attested</u> by the experience of states: lawgivers make the citizens good by training them in habits of right action—this is the aim of all legislation, and if it fails to do this it is a failure; this is what distinguishes a good form of constitution from a bad one” (1996, 1103b20).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 attested와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: attested=입증된 / confirmed=확인된 / denied=부인된 / hidden=숨겨진 / delayed=지연된
det.analysis:
① confirmed: 확인된 — attested(입증된)의 동의어 ←정답

② denied: 부인된 — attested와 반대예요

③ hidden: 숨겨진 — 드러냄의 반대라 의미가 달라요

④ delayed: 지연된 — 시간이라 의미축이 달라요
det.tip: This truth is attested by the experience of states = 입증되다 → confirmed.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ancient와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: ancient=고대의 / distant=먼 / foreign=외국의 / sacred=신성한 / modern=현대의
det.analysis:
① distant: 먼 — 거리라 의미축이 달라요

② foreign: 외국의 — 지역이라 의미가 달라요

③ sacred: 신성한 — 종교·가치라 의미축이 달라요

④ modern: 현대의 — ancient(고대의)의 반의어 ←정답
det.tip: ancient Greece ↔ modern(현대의).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 constant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: constant=끊임없는 / occasional=가끔의 / frequent=잦은 / endless=끝없는 / rapid=빠른
det.analysis:
① occasional: 가끔의 — constant(끊임없는)의 반의어 ←정답

② frequent: 잦은 — 자주 일어난다는 쪽이라 반대가 아니에요

③ endless: 끝없는 — constant와 비슷한 뜻이라 함정이에요

④ rapid: 빠른 — 속도라 의미축이 달라요
det.tip: requiring constant practice ↔ occasional(가끔의).

questions.passage:
(A) In ancient Greece, each city was an independent <u>state</u> with its own laws and army.

(B) At the trial, the lawyer asked the man to <u>state</u> exactly what he had seen that night.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 state의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: state: (A) 국가(명사) (B) 진술하다(동사)
det.analysis:
① (A) 상태 (B) 진술하다: (A)는 독립된 '국가'예요

② (A) 국가 (B) 상태: (B)는 본 것을 '진술하다'예요

③ (A) 국가 (B) 진술하다: 고유한 법을 가진 독립된 '국가' + 본 것을 '진술하다' ←정답

④ (A) 진술하다 (B) 국가: 둘 다 품사가 반대예요
det.tip: an independent state = 국가 vs state what he had seen = 진술하다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a good quality or habit that a person has, especially a moral one such as honesty or courage"

det.korean: failure=실패 / virtue=미덕 / purpose=목적 / leisure=여가
det.analysis:
① failure: 실패 — 좋은 자질과 반대예요

② virtue: 미덕 — 정직·용기 같은 도덕적으로 좋은 자질 ←정답

③ purpose: 목적 — 목표라 정의와 달라요

④ leisure: 여가 — 자유 시간이라 도덕적 자질과 무관해요
det.tip: a good moral quality such as honesty → 미덕(virtue).

questions.passage: Acquiring virtue is a difficult task, __________ (require) constant practice. The acquisition of virtue necessarily involves a community to provide education, virtues, and provide opportunities for a person to behave virtuously.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: require → requiring: 앞 문장을 받아 '~하면서'를 더하는 분사구문이라 -ing로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
콤마 뒤 '__________ constant practice'는 주절(미덕을 얻는 것은 어려운 과제다)을 받아 '그래서 끊임없는 연습을 요구하면서'라는 뜻을 더하는 분사구문이에요. 주어가 능동적으로 '요구하는' 것이라 require를 현재분사 requiring으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 require를 requiring으로 써요.
det.tip: , + -ing = 분사구문(~하면서).

questions.passage: Acquiring virtue is a difficult task, requiring constant practice. The acquisition of virtue necessarily involves a community to provide education, virtues, and provide opportunities for a person to behave __________ (virtuous).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: virtuous → virtuously: 동사 behave를 꾸미는 자리라 형용사를 부사로 바꿔요 (-ly).
det.analysis:
'behave __________'에서 동사 behave 뒤에는 '어떻게 행동하는지'를 꾸미는 부사가 와요. 형용사 virtuous(덕 있는)에 -ly를 붙이면 부사 virtuously(덕 있게)가 돼요. 사람이 '덕 있게' 행동할 기회를 제공한다는 뜻이에요.

→ 따라서 virtuous를 virtuously로 써요.
det.tip: 형용사 + -ly = 부사 (동사 수식).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: constant practice=끊임없는 연습 / blind luck=순전한 운 / quiet rest=조용한 휴식 / right action=옳은 행동
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 'make the citizens good by training them in habits of ______(~의 습관으로 훈련시켜 시민을 선하게 만든다)'가 단서예요.

① constant practice: 끊임없는 연습 — 시민을 '선하게' 만드는 습관의 내용과 어울리지 않아요

② blind luck: 순전한 운 — 훈련으로 기르는 습관과 안 맞아요

③ quiet rest: 조용한 휴식 — 선한 시민을 기르는 맥락과 무관해요

④ right action: 옳은 행동 — 시민을 선하게 만드는 '옳은 행동'의 습관 ←정답
det.tip: training them in habits of ______ → 옳은 행동(right action).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: political life=정치적 삶 / good life=좋은 삶 / moral question=도덕적 물음 / city state=도시국가
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 'society is an essential part of living a good life, which involves a well-constructed __________(사회는 좋은 삶의 필수적 부분이고, 그것은 잘 구성된 ~을 포함한다)'가 단서예요.

① political life: 정치적 삶 — 아리스토텔레스는 좋은 삶이 '잘 구성된 정치적 삶'을 포함한다고 봐요 ←정답

② good life: 좋은 삶 — 바로 앞에 이미 나온 말이라 중복돼요

③ moral question: 도덕적 물음 — well-constructed와 어울리지 않아요

④ city state: 도시국가 — 좋은 삶의 구성 요소 맥락과 안 맞아요
det.tip: a good life involves a well-constructed __________ → 정치적 삶(political life).
